gcManager.articleOne: A very common practice in church life is that its members gather in small groups for the purpose of relating, sharing experiences, learning about God, among other things. As the church grows, it becomes necessary to manage these groups in some way, and the most common way is to use a spreadsheet.
gcManager.articleTwo: GC Manager is a web application that aims to facilitate the management of Growth Groups of the Angelim Teresina Church and its campuses, allowing the creation, editing, and deletion of groups, user creation, access control via permissions, etc.
gcManager.articleThreePartOne: One of the main features of this system is the ability to generate banners with the information of a GC. Not long ago, this work was done using the online tool
gcManager.articleThreePartTwo: and all the information was entered manually, which took about 8 minutes to complete. The work involved: checking the GC data in a previously filled spreadsheet, adding the information to the template, and downloading the banner.
gcManager.articleFourPartOne: Later, when I took on the responsibility of updating the information of the GCs and generating the banners, I created a script using Javascript, and the time to generate a single banner dropped to less than 1 second! The script fetched the GC information from a file
gcManager.articleFourPartTwo: exported from a Google Sheets spreadsheet and generated the image using the library
gcManager.articleFourPartThree: along with the Node.js File System module. This mini project significantly reduced the time spent when I needed to generate banners in bulk and was used for a long time.
gcManager.articleFive: This only solved part of the problem. Now, it is necessary for other people to manage this, hence the need for a system that facilitates this work and is available, preferably on the internet.
gcManager.articleSixListOneItemOne: Clear separation of responsibilities: business logic (Model), user interface (View), and data flow control (Controller).
gcManager.articleSixListOneItemTwo: Facilitates maintenance, scalability, and testability of the system.
gcManager.articleSixListOneItemThree: Makes the code more organized and easier to understand, ideal for projects that may grow or have multiple developers involved.
gcManager.articleSixListTwoItemOne: Isolated and replicable environment: the system can run on any machine with Docker, ensuring that all developers and environments use the same configuration.
gcManager.articleSixListTwoItemTwo: Ease of configuring dependencies, such as databases and auxiliary services, using docker-compose.
gcManager.articleSixListTwoItemThree: Prepared for deployment in containers, facilitating the transition between development, testing, and production.
gcManager.articleSixListThreeItemOne: Management of changes in the database structure via migrations, maintaining history and full control over modifications.
gcManager.articleSixListThreeItemTwo: Automatic synchronization between environments (development, staging, and production), avoiding conflicts or inconsistencies.
gcManager.articleSixListThreeItemTree: Ease of reverting changes, if necessary, with security and predictability.
gcManager.articleSixListFourItemOne: Use of Prettier to ensure consistent and automated code formatting.
gcManager.articleSixListFourItemTwo: Linting with defined rules, helping to avoid common errors and follow best development practices.
gcManager.articleSixListFourItemTree: Standardized commits with Conventional Commits, facilitating the reading of the change history and integrating with versioning tools and automations (such as changelog generation).
gcManager.articleSixListFiveItemOne: Unit test coverage to ensure that each isolated part of the system works as expected.
gcManager.articleSixListFiveItemTwo: Integration tests to validate the behavior between the modules and services of the system.
gcManager.articleSixListFiveItemTree: Automated execution of tests as part of the development process, contributing to safer and more agile deliveries.
gcManager.articleSixListSixItemOne: Secure authentication system with encrypted password storage.
gcManager.articleSixListSixItemTwo: Permission-based access control, allowing different user profiles to have differentiated accesses.
gcManager.articleSixListSixItemTree: Route protection to ensure that only authorized users access certain parts of the system.
gcManager.articleSixListSevenItemTwo: Custom error messages displayed appropriately to facilitate user experience.
gcManager.articleSixListSevenItemTree: Support for multiple environments (development, staging, production).
